chunks: From him, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, upon them be peace.

Regarding a man who freed a female slave while she was pregnant, and he specified the one in her womb, he said: 'The female slave is free, and the one in her womb is free, because the one in her womb is from her.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on freeing a pregnant slave woman and her unborn child in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq clarifies that the fetus is legally an extension of the mother, meaning manumission of the mother automatically confers freedom to the unborn child, a principle known as 'itq al-um' in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the status of the child as a freeborn (hur) from the moment of the mother's emancipation, distinguishing it from cases where the child might remain in bondage if the mother were not freed. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the continuity of legal status between mother and offspring in the context of manumission.
